author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Luigi Mangione, who had always protested his innocence, pleaded guilty in federal court in Lower Manhattan to killing UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson on December 4, 2024. He described suffering years of pain from a back injury and frustration with the American healthcare industry, saying he learned of a UnitedHealthcare company convention, waited outside for Thompson to arrive, and shot him, knowing it was illegal. His lawyer, Karen Friedman Agnifilo, called it "a solemn and significant day," saying Mangione has accepted full responsibility. 

The case drew major publicity in part over Mangione's stance against the US healthcare industry, where 28 million people cannot get or afford insurance, but federal prosecutor Jamie McDonald said that was no excuse, calling the killing "deliberate, calculated and premeditated." 

Al Jazeera's Richard Gaisford reports from New York.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Israeli settlers have surrounded three Palestinian homes in Qusra, in the Occupied West Bank, cutting off water and electricity and trapping Palestinian families inside. 

The siege has lasted for days, with security camera footage showing settlers surrounding the properties, erecting tents and at times attempting to break in. 

Palestinian families say they live in constant fear, while children are afraid to leave their parents’ side. Israeli forces have also been filmed joining settlers in morning prayers rather than dispersing them, while soldiers told Palestinian families to leave their homes. 

The families have since moved into one of the three homes, fearing they would not be able to return. 

Settlers have also blocked ambulances and people bringing food, leaving basic supplies running low. The standoff has drawn growing international attention and condemnation.

Al Jazeera’s Perry Wilton reports on the situation in Qusra.

description:
Russia's economy has held up longer than many expected, defying Western sanctions.

But four years into the Russia-Ukraine war, the strain is starting to bite. Growth is forecast to slow to its weakest pace since 2022. The budget deficit is widening. And Ukrainian strikes are reaching deeper into the economy.

Even so, Moscow's pockets remain deep, with more than $300bn in accessible reserves. The US-Israel war on Iran has handed it a windfall, sending energy prices higher and boosting Moscow's revenues.

The United States has moved to cut that off, with the US Senate backing tariffs of up to 100 percent on Russian energy buyers.

description:
A wing of Cali’s largest university hospital collapsed after an earthquake, trapping children and adults, including patients recovering from surgery. 

Families have waited outside the hospital for days, demanding information about their loved ones as rescue efforts continue.

Officials have confirmed that people have died inside the collapsed building, but families are still hoping for survivors. Confusion and disorganisation have added to the anguish, with some relatives receiving conflicting information about missing family members.

The Legal Institute, which serves as a morgue, has also been forced to operate from tents after its own building was deemed unsafe. Colombia’s president is expected to visit Cali and other badly affected areas, including Chocó, the earthquake’s epicentre.

Al Jazeera’s Lucia Newman reports from Cali, Colombia.

description:
Cities across Ukraine are facing near-daily Russian attacks, with 11 locations hit overnight on Thursday, including Sumy, Zaporizhzhia, Odesa and Kramatorsk. Several people were killed and more than two dozen wounded, including children. Ukraine says more than 100 drones were launched, but it is no longer releasing figures for missiles used, citing security concerns and shortages of interceptor missiles.

Ukraine’s grain industry is also suffering from repeated Russian attacks on ports. Hundreds of vessels have been targeted by both sides in the Black Sea over the past month, prompting Ukraine to propose a ceasefire covering civilian vessels. Kyiv says this would allow ports to reopen and farmers to export their harvest during a crucial period. Russia has not yet responded to the proposal.

Al Jazeera’s Audrey McAlpin  reports from Kyiv.

Friday’s drone attack on the Ust-Luga port in Russia’s Leningrad region marks at least the sixth time this year that the critical energy hub has been targeted.

Ust-Luga is Russia’s largest Baltic Sea energy hub and a vital pipeline and shipping terminal for crude oil and petroleum products. Ukraine says its strikes are cutting into the multimillion-dollar export revenues Moscow uses to fund its war economy.

The latest strike triggered a fire at the port, which regional officials said was quickly extinguished. No casualties were reported. 

Meanwhile, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov says Russia is not prepared to stop hostilities along the current combat line because its war goals have not yet been achieved.

Al Jazeera’s Yulia Shapovalova reports from Moscow.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Venezuela possesses some of the world’s largest proven oil reserves, but much of its oil industry remains in disrepair.

After Nicolas Maduro’s removal, Washington eased some energy restrictions in the hope that American investment would help revive Venezuela’s struggling oil sector. Venezuela’s interim government also moved to open the industry to greater foreign investment.

But no major American reconstruction projects have come online. Years of underinvestment, sanctions, corruption and deteriorating infrastructure have left wells, pipelines and refineries requiring extensive rebuilding.

Industry analysts estimate that rebuilding the sector could cost more than $100bn over the next 15 years. Commercial uncertainty, political instability, legal hurdles and questions over future policy are also making investors hesitant.

description: From opposition figure to Head of State - how Ahmed al Sharaa plans to transform Syria into a modern Arab democracy. In this extended interview, Al Jazeera’s Ali Al Dafiri talks to al-Sharaa about his plans for Syria. In December 2024, the 53-year rule by the al-Assad dynasty crumbled in the face of overwhelming armed opposition, led by Abu Mohammed al-Julani, leader of Hayat Tahrir al-Sham. Bashar al-Assad was forced out of office and fled to Russia - and al-Julani took power to become President Ahmed al-Sharaa. In the months that followed, he re-established diplomatic relations between Syria and the regional and global community that had fractured over previous decades. Al Dafiri asks al-Sharaa about his plans to revitalise his country, where economic progress and social development had come to a standstill due to continued Western sanctions and increasing isolation. Al-Sharaa reveals a potential security agreement with Israel - and says he’ll play no part in military action in Leba

description: An independent body has launched hearings into killings connected to former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte's anti-drugs campaign. The government says about 6,000 people were killed, but rights groups say the death toll from extrajudicial killings by police and suspected vigilantes may be as high as 30,000. Luzviminda Siapo testified on the first day of hearings about her disabled teenage son Raymart, abducted and killed nine years ago while she worked abroad in Kuwait. Forensic pathologist Dr Raquel Fortun, a commission member, says an examination of his remains suggests he was shot at close range. Duterte is currently on trial at the International Criminal Court for crimes against humanity linked to the drug war, though few cases have reached local courts. author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Colombians are continuing the desperate search for victims and possible survivors of Monday's devastating magnitude 7.4 earthquake. Almost 4,000 people were injured, and at least 281 have been killed, a number expected to rise as more bodies are recovered. By day four, the critical 72-hour window for finding survivors alive had long passed, and rescue teams called off the search for one trapped person at 3am after the last signs of life disappeared. Unlike other countries in the region that have faced similar disasters, Colombia's new government, in office for less than a week, has refused to allow trained international search-and-rescue teams, including those from Mexico, to help, a decision confirmed by Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum. Survivors who lost everything are now sleeping in parks, relying on donations from churches, NGOs and ordinary citizens rather than the government. 

Al Jazeera's Latin America editor Lucia Newman reports from Pereira.

title: Colombia earthquake search ends as government declines foreign help

description:
The ballot papers are nearly a metre long, with an unprecedented 34 candidates taking part in this special constituency election, and only one representing a mainstream political party. That's Nigel Farage, leader of the anti-immigrant Reform UK party and a man often tipped as a future British prime minister, who finds himself in a predicament of his own making, having resigned his parliamentary seat in Clacton last month over questions about his financial affairs, including a multimillion-dollar gift he failed to declare. He'd hoped to trigger a contest billed as the people against the establishment. Instead it's become Farage against a host of unlikely candidates, including Count Binface, a man in a spacesuit wearing a dustbin on his head. The parliamentary investigation into his finances is on hold but could resume immediately, potentially leading to his suspension or another, far more seriously contested by-election over the seat. 

Al Jazeera's Jonah Hull reports from Clacton.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Votes are being counted in Zambia's presidential and parliamentary elections, widely seen as a test for President Hakainde Hichilema's economic policies, following a campaign dominated by concern over rising living costs. Hichilema took office in 2021 and steered Zambia through a debt restructuring and recovery, but many voters remain concerned about the high cost of living, unemployment and an unstable electricity supply. His main challenger, Brian Mundubile, a first-time presidential candidate backed by a coalition of opposition parties, hopes to capitalise on that frustration. A candidate needs more than 50 percent of the vote to win outright, otherwise the two leading contenders will face a run-off within 37 days. Officials are calling on voters to remain calm as they await the outcome, with final results expected on Monday. Al Jazeera's Haru Mutasa reports.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Russia says a Ukrainian drone attack has targeted a region around 2,000km from the border. Ukraine's military says it hit an oil refinery and petrochemical complex there. Russia's largest online retailer, Wildberries, says the strikes also caused a fire in an industrial area where one of its warehouses is located, forcing an evacuation of employees, though no retail goods had been stored there. Ukraine's campaign against Wildberries has destroyed more than a third of its warehouse capacity since mid-July, inflicting billions of dollars in losses; because the company doesn't insure against drone damage, some independent sellers have been left without revenue. To cope with the fallout, the Kremlin has rolled back environmental standards to allow the sale of low-grade Euro-2 fuel through 2027 and was forced to import its first emergency petrol shipment from India.

Al Jazeera's Yulia Shapovalova reports from Moscow.
